title: Rage Bait: How Online Anger Makes Money

blanks.sentence: Rage bait refers to online material created to make users feel _____.
A provocative post can attract reactions, raise traffic and bring financial _____ to the creator.
Some creators chase more _____ because payment rises with audience numbers.
The reactions can still be profitable even when they are _____.
A normal marketing hook should reflect the content accurately and be based on _____.
Unlike a trustworthy hook, rage bait relies on _____ to influence users.
Influencers exploit _____ so that users pay more attention to certain content.
Algorithmic amplification can finally lead to more _____.
Biases are often not deliberate; they may be _____ feelings for or against an idea.
By provoking emotions, creators are more likely to capture users’ _____.

multipleChoice.question: What distinguishes rage bait from ordinary attention-grabbing online content at the beginning of the discussion?
options: It mainly uses celebrity gossip to encourage curiosity.
It is deliberately designed to produce anger or outrage.
It usually asks users to compare different political views.
It depends on software that blocks emotional reactions.

multipleChoice.question: According to the explanation, what usually happens after people react angrily to a provocative post?
options: The creator immediately removes the original post.
The post becomes less visible because users dislike it.
The audience stops sharing similar content.
The content receives wider attention and traffic.

multipleChoice.question: What commercial logic does Andrea Jones identify behind some creators’ behaviour?
options: Higher engagement can mean higher payment.
Negative comments usually reduce creators’ income.
Creators are paid only when users feel positive.
Marketing platforms ban content that causes anger.

multipleChoice.question: How does Andrea contrast a marketing hook with rage-baiting content?
options: A hook is usually longer, while rage bait is usually shorter.
A hook avoids emotion, while rage bait avoids online sharing.
A hook should honestly match the content, while rage bait manipulates users.
A hook is used by amateurs, while rage bait is used by professionals.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Andrea’s view imply that rage bait is worse than clickbait?
options: It is less truthful and tries to influence people for its own advantage.
It is mainly unsuccessful at attracting online reactions.
It only works when users already agree with the creator.
It is used mostly to teach marketing clients about trust.

multipleChoice.question: What does Dr Brady suggest influencers try to exploit?
options: Users’ technical knowledge of algorithms.
Users’ desire to avoid advertising.
Users’ ability to detect fake headlines.
Users’ psychological biases that guide attention.

multipleChoice.question: In Dr Brady’s explanation, what is the role of algorithms?
options: They judge whether comments are morally acceptable.
They amplify content that people are likely to notice.
They prevent creators from earning advertising money.
They remove emotional posts from social platforms.

multipleChoice.question: What does the informal word “eyeballs” refer to in this context?
options: People who produce angry online comments.
The emotional biases behind a reaction.
People viewing online content.
The visual design of a social media post.

multipleChoice.question: Why can emotional content be especially effective?
options: Human beings have evolved to pay attention to emotions.
Users are unable to recognise any emotional manipulation.
Algorithms only promote content with positive emotions.
Creators are usually unaware that emotions affect users.

multipleChoice.question: What practical response is suggested for users who encounter outrageous content?
options: Share it quickly so others can judge it.
Comment angrily to reduce its reach.
Follow creators who post more extreme examples.
Pause and think before reacting or sharing.
